name: feed-driven-teaser-list
display_name: Teaser list rendered from a data feed, with an honest openable/inert split
description: A list whose rows are cloned from a hidden template and filled from a feed. Whether a row is a control is decided by the DATA, not by the template: a row whose record carries the linked content becomes a real link; a row whose record does not is stripped of the template's placeholder href and left out of the tab order.

contract.outcome: the row is a real control: it carries a genuine href and remains keyboard-reachable; what activation DOES is the referencing journey's clause, not this component's
contract.note: this component contract stops at 'is a control / is not a control'. The behaviour behind the control belongs to a micro-journey entry that requires this contract (here: teaser-detail-deeplink).

_SCHEMA_DELTA: states / data_contract / degraded_states are fields the draft DDL does not have — see HARVEST_01 §3.

states.condition: the row's feed record lacks the field the linked content lives in
states.outcome: the row shows its teaser text and is visibly not offered as openable
states.why: the template ships a placeholder href='#'. Cloning it for a row with nowhere to go MANUFACTURES a dead control — the defect class this workstream exists to stop (bugs_open/023; the 2026-07-22 gauntlet correction). Stripping it is not cosmetic: it is the contract.
states.evidence: archive_loader_new.js --static branch removes href AND tabindex; live check B.3; feed carries 7 openable + 1 inert, so the split is exercised by real data

must: have its own href removed before any clone is appended
states.why: the un-cloned template is itself markup on the page; left with href='#' it is a dead control that no visitor can see but every sweep can find
states.evidence: archive_loader_new.js: tmpl.removeAttribute("href") before the clone loop

states.outcome: the empty-state line remains visible; it is hidden only after at least one row renders

data_contract.absence_semantics: a missing optional field hides its slot rather than rendering an orphan separator — vonc: the stat dot is hidden when the entry has no stat, because there are no invented participation numbers any more

degraded_states.outcome: the shell and the empty state are left exactly as built — no half-populated rows, no invented error UI

item_openable_selector.reason: Serves the openable/inert split — the entry's most valuable clause. Declared but not referenced by any check because no attribute assertion exists at either tier, so 'this element does/does not carry the attribute' cannot be checked. Kept so the requirement survives until the harness can run it — deleting it would delete the record of what the clause needs.

empty_state_selector.reason: Serves the degraded 'feed empty' clause. Declared but not referenced by any check because no empty-region assertion exists; innerText on a display:none subtree falls back to textContent, so 'nothing is shown here' is not checkable today. Kept so the requirement survives until the harness can run it — deleting it would delete the record of what the clause needs.

checks.note: asserts existence; selector_count is existence-only at both tiers, and min=1 added nothing

checks._unsupported: same gap; this one is invisible to a human reviewer, which is exactly why it wants a machine check
